documents.title: Nephrology follow-up letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Mr. Dabrowski, now 67, returned 1/7/2020. His tiredness and stamina have kept getting worse since he saw hematology. He has had no bleeding or dark stools and his eating hasn't changed.

BP 150/92. Conjunctivae pale; the rest of the exam is normal, including a normal neurologic exam.

Labs: creatinine 3.0 mg/dL, steady. Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, hematocrit 30%, MCV 85 fL. Ferritin 230 ng/mL, iron 40 mcg/dL.

Assessment: CKD stage 4 from diabetic nephropathy, stable; symptomatic anemia of CKD with adequate iron stores.

Plan: start darbepoetin alfa 40 mcg subcutaneously every 2 weeks, given in our infusion area, with hemoglobin checks monthly at first and a target of 10 to 11.5. Blood pressure is above goal today; please recheck at your next visit as ESAs can raise it. No other changes.

Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, sevelamer carbonate 800 mg three times daily with meals, calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed, now darbepoetin as above.

Nephrology

documents.title: Darbepoetin coverage
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Nephrology office called to ask for our last two hemoglobin results for his darbepoetin coverage paperwork. Faxed 11/13/18 CBC and the 12/24/18 hematology letter. They say the first dose is scheduled next week.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Nephrology started darbepoetin every two weeks, two doses so far. He thinks he's a little less wiped out. Home BP he doesn't check.

Exam: BP per flowsheet. Pale but less so. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: numbness unchanged, skin intact.

A/P: anemia of CKD now on ESA - nephrology drawing monthly. HTN - recheck today as nephrology asked; continue lisinopril 10. DM2 - A1c in December was in his usual range. Back in 3 months.

documents.title: COVID check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Outreach call to high-risk patients. He's staying home, daughter dropping off groceries. Has 90 days of all meds. Still going to nephrology for his injections; they screen at the door. No symptoms. Converted May visit to video.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from home, identity verified, consent for video. Daughter helped set up the tablet.

Feels better than in the winter, energy up since the injections. Sugars by his log 130s-180s. No lows. Smoking more being stuck at home, he admits. Feet: checks them every night, nothing new.

Exam limited to video: comfortable, speaking full sentences, no visible distress.

A/P: chronic issues stable. Labs at the nephrology draw. In-person visit in late summer if things allow. Smoking - offered patch by mail, not now.

Continue darbepoetin 40 mcg every 2 weeks with monthly hemoglobin. Other medications unchanged.

Plan: A1c, lipids, UACR. Eye exam next week. Flu shot in October.

orders.reason: Diabetic plantar ulcer, right foot, with neuropathy

documents.title: Foot ulcer
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Noticed a spot on the ball of his right foot about a month ago when checking his feet. Doesn't hurt (feet are numb). No drainage he's seen, no fever.

Exam: R plantar surface under the 1st metatarsal head, round ulcer about 1.5 cm with a thick callus rim, clean pink base, no drainage, no surrounding redness or warmth, no odor. No crepitus. L foot intact. DP faint both sides. Monofilament absent at most sites.

A/P
1. Diabetic foot ulcer R, neuropathic - referred to podiatry this month for debridement and offloading. Keep weight off it as best he can, clean dressing daily. Call for redness, drainage, fever.
2. Vaccines: high-dose flu and second PPSV23 (5 years after the first) today.
3. Due A1c next month, lab visit booked.

documents.title: Podiatry consultation
documents.author: podiatry
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Dabrowski on 10/27/2020 for a plantar ulcer under the right first metatarsal head, present about two months.

Exam: neuropathic ulcer about 1.8 cm with hyperkeratotic rim. After sharp debridement of the callus the base is granular, no exposed tendon or bone, no probe to deep structures today. No cellulitis. Protective sensation absent both feet. Dorsalis pedis pulses diminished.

Plan: sharp debridement done today. Offloading surgical shoe with a felt aperture pad. Saline and foam dressing changed daily. Return in 2 weeks and then every 2 to 4 weeks.

NKDA.

Podiatry

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stan, your A1c came back 9.2, the highest it's been since you joined us. High sugars slow wound healing, so this matters for your foot. Let's get back to the basics we talked about: fewer sweets and juice, smaller portions at dinner, and your glargine every single night. Kidney numbers were steady. I'll send the result to podiatry.

conditions.label: Other chronic osteomyelitis, right ankle and foot

reports.text: Right foot, three views. Soft tissue defect at the plantar aspect of the first metatarsal head. Cortical erosion and loss of the subchondral outline along the plantar first metatarsal head. No fracture. No soft tissue gas. Joint spaces otherwise preserved.
reports.conclusion: Cortical erosion of the right first metatarsal head beneath the ulcer, consistent with osteomyelitis in this setting.

documents.title: Podiatry follow-up
documents.author: podiatry
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Mr. Dabrowski returned on 12/28/2020. The right plantar ulcer has been open about three months and has slowly enlarged despite offloading. He feels a dull ache there at times but no fever or chills. Your most recent A1c was 9.2%.

Exam: ulcer 3 cm across with a calloused margin and only slight redness around it. No pus. Probe reaches bone at the base. Sensation decreased in a stocking-glove pattern. Dorsalis pedis pulses diminished on both sides.

Labs: WBC 7,500/uL, hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, ESR 70 mm/hr, CRP 25 mg/L.

X-ray: erosion of the plantar cortex of the first metatarsal head.

Assessment: osteomyelitis of the right first metatarsal head under a chronic diabetic neuropathic ulcer.

Plan: percutaneous bone biopsy done in clinic for pathology and culture; antibiotics to be chosen on the culture. Continue offloading and dressings. I will call you with the result.

NKDA.

Podiatry

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 6 weeks

reports.text: Specimen: bone, right first metatarsal head, needle biopsy. Microscopic: fragments of necrotic trabecular bone with marrow fibrosis and a mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes and plasma cells. No malignancy.

documents.title: Podiatry call re: biopsy
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Podiatry called with bone biopsy: chronic osteomyelitis, culture grew methicillin-susceptible S. aureus. They have prescribed cephalexin 500 mg twice daily for 6 weeks, dose adjusted for his kidneys, started today. Weekly wound checks there. Path and culture reports faxed and scanned. Routed to PCP; appointment 1/12 already on the books.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Podiatry note and biopsy reviewed: osteomyelitis of the R 1st metatarsal head, MSSA, on cephalexin 500 BID x 6 weeks since 1/5. ESR 70, CRP 25 on 12/28. Taking the antibiotic, some loose stools, no rash. In the surgical shoe.

Exam: afebrile. R foot dressed, not taken down (podiatry saw it yesterday). No proximal redness, no calf tenderness.

A/P
1. Osteomyelitis R foot - on list. Cephalexin through mid-February. BMP today with his kidneys on the antibiotic.
2. DM2 - A1c 9.2 in November. Diet reviewed again; glargine 24 nightly. Repeat A1c spring.
3. Anemia of CKD - Hgb 13.2 at podiatry draw, above nephrology's target; their letter pending.
4. COVID vaccine - eligible, signed up through the state site, daughter helping.

documents.body:
AWV. Independent at home. No falls this year. Uses a handrail on the cellar stairs. PHQ-2 0. Proxy on file (daughter).

This year: osteomyelitis R foot treated and healed; COVID primary series done.

Preventive: high-dose flu and Pfizer booster today. Lung CT next month, ordered. Colonoscopy due 2024. Eye exam August, no retinopathy. Tdap due next year (Td 2012).

Tobacco: offered help again; declined.

RTC 3-4 months.
